1) Legal hold: is this convo subject to any litigation or regulatory hold? If yes, we cannot remove until the hold is lifted — please confirm in writing.
2) Scope: do you want the deletion to be limited to the conversation body and activity indexes, or should we also schedule an erasure pass for secondary backups/nearline copies?

Technical note: targeted erasure is surgical but irreversible. It will scrub message bodies, activity indexes, and telemetry references; however, offline backups and long-term archival snapshots are handled by a separate erase pipeline and take longer.

If you can confirm no legal hold and attach signed authorization, I will schedule the deletion window and post an exact ETA.

Adding technical details for the run (for the record):

- Targets: activity index entries, per-message payloads, telemetry events mapped to convo-ff72a8c, and any cached search indices.
- Exclusions by default: cold tape/backups older than retention window (we will need an additional erase job to touch offline backups).
- Steps: 1) lock the conversation id to prevent new writes; 2) remove message payloads and delete index pointers; 3) run index compaction; 4) kick separate backups erase job (if authorized).
- Estimated time: index removal + compaction for a single convo: 2–6 hours depending on queue position. Backup/nearline erasure: 3–5 business days (requires targeted overwrite / manifest update).
- Audit: we will produce a redaction audit entry (redacted record indicating action taken) and an immutable audit ticket with the support case. The redacted entry notes that content was removed for a compliance request — it will not include the original PII.

Risks/notes: if the convo appears in any exported logs previously delivered to your systems (S3 buckets, splunk, etc.), we cannot control copies you already hold — please coordinate with your infra team.

I'll standby for signed authorization. Once received, I will reserve a deletion slot and confirm ETA.

— Vivek
